messages.content: Predict the observed decision of a human responder in a one-shot anonymous two-player bargaining game. The proposer privately knows the actual initial amount of money. The proposer first reports an amount to the responder; that report may be truthful or misleading. The proposer then offers a monetary amount to the responder. The responder now chooses whether to accept or reject the offer. All stated amounts are US cents. If accepted, the responder earns the offered amount and the proposer earns the actual initial amount minus the offer. If rejected, both receive zero from this game. A fixed participation payment is separate from these game earnings. The responder sees the reported initial amount and the offer, and has not yet been shown the actual initial amount or the eventual outcome. This is a single interaction without role switching or previous-round feedback. Age and gender, when supplied, are the responder's own stable self-reports collected after the game; later psychological questionnaires and outcome ratings are not prediction features. Output only accept or reject, without an explanation.

You are the responder. The proposer reported an initial amount of 30 cents and now offers you 15 cents. Your own self-reported age is 65 years. Your own self-reported gender is female. Predict whether you accept or reject the offer.
accept
